posts.title: The sweet potato harvest
posts.excerpt: Thirty-one children, four rows and one very large potato.
posts.content:
The garden class planted sweet potato slips in May and watered them all summer. On Tuesday they dug them up with their hands and small trowels, and the biggest one needed three children to lift.

Our cook baked them for Friday’s snack. Please send boots and a change of trousers next week too: the beds still need clearing before we sow onions.

posts.title: Starting in April: a short guide
posts.excerpt: Visits, applications and the first two weeks, in order.
posts.content:
Applications for April open on 15 October. Come to a visit morning first, then fill in the form at the front desk or by email. We reply to every family by the end of November.

The first two weeks are gentle: one hour with a parent, then mornings, then full days. Every child has a key teacher, and you will get a written note each evening about how the day went.

posts.title: Friday cooking with the studio class
posts.excerpt: Washing, weighing and a soup for eighty-four.
posts.content:
Every Friday six children from the studio class join our cook for an hour. This week they washed carrots from the garden, weighed them on the kitchen scales and counted out bowls for every room.

The soup was served at lunch with rice and pear. The menu for each month hangs by the front door, and we mark every dish that contains common allergens.
